signals.signal: 50-60% of viewers who drop off do so within the first 3 seconds; Shorts with immediate hook in first 2 seconds retain 19% more viewers.
signals.raw_quote: 50-60% of viewers who drop off do so within the first 3 seconds. More significantly, Shorts with an immediate hook in the first 2 seconds retain 19% more viewers, and over 80% of all engagement happens within the first 10 seconds.

signals.signal: 3-part hook structure: visual hook + 3-7 word text hook + 5-10 word verbal hook, all within 3 seconds.
signals.raw_quote: Visual hook: A surprising frame, strong emotion, unusual object, clear result, or action in progress. Show the payoff, not the setup. Text hook: 3-7 words highlighting a result, mistake, secret, or comparison. Verbal hook: 5-10 words delivering the promise clearly and directly.

signals.signal: 'Did You Know' format (knowledge-gap hook) earned 31M views for Nas Daily's poisonous book video.
signals.raw_quote: 'Did You Know That...' — Knowledge-gap approach; Nas Daily's poisonous book video earned 31M views.

signals.signal: Faceless voiceover Shorts have structural loop advantage — 58% of faceless creators reported higher retention in 2025.
signals.raw_quote: There's no face, no body language, no physical continuity cue signaling restart. The transition feels invisible to viewers, enabling stronger loop effects. 58% of faceless YouTube Shorts creators reported higher retention rates in 2025.

signals.signal: Every loop/replay counts as an additional view since March 31, 2025. Average Shorts retention is 73% vs 52% for long-form. Replay rate 10%+ = excellent, 20%+ = exceptional.
signals.raw_quote: YouTube counts each loop as an additional view, meaning a viewer watching a 20-second Short three times generates three separate views. Average Shorts retention: 73% (vs. 52% for long-form).

signals.signal: Successful Shorts in March 2026 averaged 74% VVSA in first hour; target 70%+ watch-through rate; viral Shorts (1M+ views) average 76% retention.
signals.raw_quote: Successful Shorts in March 2026 data averaged a 74 percent first-hour view velocity success average (VVSA). Target 70%+ watch-through rate, with viral Shorts with 1M+ views averaging 76% retention.

signals.signal: Shorts older than ~30 days are now much less likely to be pushed in recommendations — evergreen compounding model has ended.
signals.raw_quote: There's been a shift away from the evergreen model where a Short could keep compounding views for months, with Shorts older than roughly 30 days now much less likely to be pushed in recommendations.

signals.signal: YouTube now distinguishes 'Engaged Views' (meaningful watch time + interaction) from basic views for YPP and monetization eligibility.
signals.raw_quote: YouTube now distinguishes between two types of metrics: Engaged Views (when the viewer interacts meaningfully, watches beyond a few seconds, likes, comments, etc.) with only Engaged Views counting toward critical metrics such as YouTube Partner Program (YPP) eligibility and revenue payouts.

signals.signal: Optimal length for educational/fact content: 25-45 seconds. A 30-second Short at 85% completion outperforms 60-second at 50% watch rate.
signals.raw_quote: Fact/educational content: 25–45 seconds maximum. A 30-second short with ~85% completion typically outperforms a 60-second video with ~50% watch rate.

signals.signal: Change visuals every 2-4 seconds; add micro open loops every 5-8 seconds in middle section; trim all pauses to zero.
signals.raw_quote: Change something every 1-2 seconds (shot size, overlay, angle, pace). Use micro open loops every 5-8 seconds.

signals.signal: YouTube Shorts algorithm no longer cares about channel size — viewer response signals (completion, replays, hook hold rate) drive distribution at any subscriber count.
signals.raw_quote: YouTube Shorts doesn't care about your channel size as much as it cares about viewer response.
